source.title: ANNEX A to Treasury Outturn Report 2025-26 — Audit & Governance Committee, 27 July 2026

facts.note: The parent Treasury Outturn Report itself (loan-book table, CFR movement, prudential indicators, investment performance) is NOT held. The annex carries no council-specific figure — only Arlingclose's UK/global commentary. Cotswold's own numbers used below all come from the companion Draft Statement of Accounts 2025/26 (16364) presented to the same committee.

source.title: Draft Statement of Accounts 2025/26 — Annex A (16364), Note D8

facts.note: Net movement in the year £89,282. The D8 explanatory note says the 2025/26 increase 'represents capital expenditure in respect of solar roof panels at Trinity Road and EVCP assets financed through the Community Municipal Investment.' Figures are £ exactly, NOT £000s or £m — this is a very small CFR.

The whole £161,581 is a Community Municipal Investment retail bond used to finance the solar/EVCP investment (per D8 note). No PWLB. No LOBO. No bank loan. No maturity table. No weighted rate is disclosed because it does not need to be at this scale.

signals.headline: Cotswold holds no PWLB debt; £161,581 of external borrowing is a Community Municipal Investment retail bond for solar/EVCP; CFR is £449,219 and MRP for 2025/26 is £3,628
signals.why_it_matters: The whole council is a net investor of the order of £29m against effectively no external debt. There is no borrowing story to tell. The only live indicator breach is on the investment-side interest-rate sensitivity, driven by surplus cash — a portfolio-composition point, not a solvency or refinancing one.

summary.text:
The paper listed for the 27 July Audit & Governance Committee (16368) is a two-page Arlingclose economic-background annex — no council-specific figure appears anywhere in it. The parent Treasury Outturn Report proper is not held. Cotswold's actual numbers all come from the companion Draft Statement of Accounts 2025/26 (16364), presented to the same committee.

The reading is straightforward and the story is small. At 31 March 2026 Cotswold's CFR is £449,219, external borrowing is £161,581 (£106,544 current + £55,037 non-current), and MRP for the year is £3,628 — the whole external balance is a Community Municipal Investment retail bond raised to finance solar panels at Trinity Road and EV charge-point assets, per the D8 note. There is no PWLB debt, no LOBO, no bank loan and no maturity ladder to speak of. Cotswold does not appear in the PWLB borrower list. The balance-sheet identity ties: £449,219 − £161,581 − £0 (no lessee finance-lease payables; Cotswold is lessor to Ubico) = £287,638 of internal borrowing, corroborated to rounding by the Q3 liability-benchmark table (15510 p.4), which is negative in every forecast year through 31/03/2028.

On the other side, the council holds around £19.3m of investments plus £9.8m of cash equivalents — a substantial net investor for a district of this size. The one live indicator breach reported at Q3 is on the investment side (1% rate-sensitivity £0.79m against a £0.18m target limit) and the council explains it as surplus cash from grant income and an underspent capital programme (15510 §4.8) — a composition point, not a borrowing point.

No email drafted. There is no PWLB story to open with, no refinancing risk, no LOBO, no discount, no dated assumption to test, and no borrowing-side indicator to comment on. Leading with a £161k retail bond or a £3.6k MRP would be padded. The council's finance function is run through Publica Group — a Publica email address for a treasury contact here is expected, not an error — and the S151 (David Stanley, Deputy Chief Executive and S151 Officer) and Deputy S151 (Michelle Burge, Chief Accountant) are named with council addresses on the SoA cover report (16363 p.1). Revisit if a paper with something distinctive appears — e.g. a plan to borrow to fund the facilities-planning capital programme trailed in the 6 and 12 August 2026 cabinet/council papers, which are on disk but not read here.

status.note: The 27 July annex is two pages of Arlingclose economic commentary with no Cotswold-specific figure. Companion SoA (16364) read and the balance sheet identity proven. Cotswold holds no PWLB, is a net investor, and the whole external-borrowing balance is a £161k retail bond. No email drafted — no first-contact hook that would land with an S151 without padding. Revisit if a facilities-planning borrowing plan (6/12 August 2026 cabinet/council papers) turns into a treasury paper we can read.
